messages:
sam-plat: Quick question — when users create an A/B in Console, what are the default safety thresholds we should surface for variant rollout? currently thinking: 1) max percent per variant, 2) min traffic before metric evaluation, 3) automatic rollback on error rate spike. Thoughts?

lia-product: Agree with those. Also we need a required metric contract for every experiment: metric id, aggregation (p95/p50/mean), direction (lower is better), and a min sample size & minimum baseline. Without that we can't surface reliable deltas.

toni-ux: UX note: surface the min-sample-size as both a numeric and a time window (e.g., "at least 1k requests OR 10 minutes, whichever comes first") so PMs don't set absurdly low numbers. show an inline estimate of time-to-eval based on current traffic. :eyes:

mike-eng: From infra side we need to lock down route-update semantics. Proposal: routing update is atomic at the routing-service layer and evaluated against guards in this order: capacity guard -> quota guard -> metric-safety guard. If any guard trips, roll back to previous routing config and emit an event.

zoe-sre: +1 to atomic. Also, telemetry needs to tag rollout events with rollout_id, variant_id, snapshot(hash) and pre/post token throughput and error rate. Otherwise postmortems are painful. Can we include those fields in the rollout event schema?

sam-plat: @lia-product + @mike-eng good point. How strict should the metric contract be? e.g., if someone picks a low-traffic route and sets p95 as the primary metric, do we block creation or just warn?

lia-product: Block on critical mismatches (e.g., p95 on <100 samples per evaluation window) — we should prevent experiments that will be meaningless. For non-critical ones show a prominent warning and require extra confirmation.

toni-ux: UI microflow: in creation wizard, step 2 = "metrics & guards". If the metric contract is invalid, show an interstitial modal that explains why and suggests fixes (switch to rate, increase min-sample-size, or pick a different metric).

mike-eng: Implementation sketch for a guard snippet we can include in Console's schema:
```json
{
  "variants": [
    {"id": "v0", "weight": 0.01},
    {"id": "v1", "weight": 0.99}
  ],
  "guards": {
    "min_sample_size": 100,
    "min_window_secs": 600,
    "max_variant_pct": 0.25,
    "rollback_on_error_rate_delta_pct": 200
  }
}
```
Note: rollback_on_error_rate_delta_pct = percent increase over baseline that triggers rollback. default 200% (i.e., triple).

zoe-sre: Love the rollback field. But we should include "lookback_baseline_window" and a flag for "use_control_only_baseline" for A/Bs where control is more stable.

sam-plat: Operational question: should Console create experiments that use dynamic routing (server-side splitters) vs static weights in the routing table? dynamic gives feature flags + better targeting but is heavier.

mike-eng: We should default to static weighted routing for simple %, and offer an "advanced" toggle for dynamic. Dynamic mode requires evaluation hooks and per-request tagging, which we can only enable if the customer's infra supports it. Console should validate compatibility.

lia-product: Also add cost guard: estimate incremental token usage and show expected monthly delta. some teams will want an upfront cost guard that refuses to exceed X% of baseline spend.

toni-ux: We'll need small inline explainer copy: "Why do we need metric contracts?" with examples. Also a compact summary card that shows expected time to statistical significance given current traffic.

sam-plat: For API/contract: Console should call the rollout service with a single payload and get back a rollout_id + predicted-risk score. rollout service evaluates guards synchronously and returns accept/soft-fail/hard-fail. soft-fail = allowed with confirmation. hard-fail = blocked.

mike-eng: That matches our plan. We'll add a new endpoint POST /rollouts/v1/plan that returns { rollout_id, status, reasons: [...], risk_score, estimated_eval_time_secs }. Console uses that to drive UX and the confirm modal.

zoe-sre: Please include a "dry_run": true option so we can validate experiments in staging without affecting routing tables.

deploy-bot: deploy noted: routing-service#3922 rolled out to staging. Use dry_run=true for testing. :white_check_mark:

sam-plat: Next steps: mike, can you draft the /plan API contract and the guard schema? lia & toni will draft the modal language and the Console wizard changes. zoe will add telemetry fields. I'll sync with PMs and legal about cost guard wording. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
